Sentence (English): There is a rumor that Siemens has a tradition of selling defective products to outsiders, but it is never better than seeing it.
Comments (English): There is a rumor that Siemens has a tradition of selling defective products to outsiders, but it is never better than seeing it. I didn’t notice the small dent on the panel of the dishwasher for a few days after I received it. After discovering it, I contacted Siemens and sent a technician to the door. After checking, the master said that he originally thought it was outside and wanted to pick it up, but he didn't expect it to be inside the machine. He had nothing to say and opened an appraisal form. After a while, I received a call from the master saying that Siemens said that his inspection order should not be opened. If it was opened, the master would be responsible for it. I was really speechless... I said there was a photo to prove it, but the photo at the time couldn't see that position, but Siemens said that their leaders and colleagues could see it... I said you can ask the master to come to the same angle and the same position. She was speechless when she took another photo... After contacting JD.com several times, the merchant only said that she was sorry and understood, but could only change the door but not the phone. I asked the customer service if you were yourself, would you do it? She was also speechless. But his attitude has always been strong and arrogant, and he will not retreat. No one can do anything about it, and there is nothing JD can do. I can only admit that I am unlucky, delete the Siemens washing and drying set from the original Jingdong shopping cart, write a negative review and move on...

After checking, the master said that he originally thought it was outside and wanted to pick it up, but he didn't expect it to be inside the machine. He had nothing to say and opened an appraisal form. After a while, I received a call from the master saying that Siemens said that his inspection order should not be opened. If it was opened, the master would be responsible for it. I was really speechless... I said there was a photo to prove it, but the photo at the time couldn't see that position, but Siemens said that their leaders and colleagues could see it... I said you can ask the master to come to the same angle and the same position. She was speechless when she took another photo... After contacting JD.com several times, the merchant only said that she was sorry and understood, but could only change the door but not the phone. I asked the customer service if you were yourself, would you do it? She was also speechless. But his attitude has always been strong and arrogant, and he will not retreat. No one can do anything about it, and there is nothing JD can do. I can only admit that I am unlucky, delete the Siemens washing and drying set from the original Jingdong shopping cart, write a negative review and move on...

Use a tape measure to check if there is space to install the lower cabinet of the 6060 standard size. 2. Although it is not indicated on the product details page, if the lower cabinet of the sink is not removed in advance or is a non-standard cabinet and needs to be reformed, the cost will be 100,000 to 200,000 won or more depending on the degree of reform. After watching YouTube and learning how to separate the lower cabinet, I finished separating the lower cabinet in advance and waited, saving 100,000 won in installation costs. It is not difficult if you loosen the 4 screws connected to the side cabinet and remove the 2 front legs, so give it a try. 3. The drain pipe joins the sink drain pipe in a Y shape, so if the drain pipe is heavily contaminated, you can prevent bad odors by replacing the drain pipe in advance. Qualifications to become friendly with the dishwasher 1. You must be someone who is not bothered by the sight of dishes piling up like a mountain in the sink. 2. If you have a lumbar joint disorder, you must bend down every time you put in and take out the dishes. 3. You must be someone who has no back problems because it will hurt. 3. Someone who has the patience to wait for 1-2 hours for the dishwashing to finish and for it to dry naturally with the door open. When you open the door, you will not see fluffy dishes and a soft interior, but rather water droplets hanging down (This is absolutely not a malfunction, and it is essential to use a tablet detergent that includes rinse to reduce the formation of water droplets.) Should I buy a 6-person or a 12-person one? 1) Who should buy a 6-person one? . If you have a lumbar joint disorder, choosing a 6-person one that can be used by placing it on the sink is good for your back health. People who have a healthy back but are neat and cannot stand seeing dishes pile up and want to wash the dishes right away. People who do not have space to install a 12-person one due to a small kitchen. 2) Who should buy a 12-person one? . A household with a family of 4 or more, where there is a lot of dishes to wash every day, or even a family of 2, who has a laid-back personality and is easygoing enough to wash a lot of dishes at once without it being an eyesore. Those who have 606084 square meters of space to install it. What is good about a 12-person media unit with all the latest features? 1. Automatic door opening function for more efficient natural drying than hot air drying 2. Height adjustment function of the single-tier, two-tier shelf allows use of large dishes or tall containers 3. 72-hour storage function allows for hygienic storage without odor or mold 4. Full stainless steel inner body for hygienic management 5. Smooth basket moving roller allows you to insert and remove baskets without much force 6. Lock mode ensures safety from child operation 7. Powerful water flow located at the upper, middle, and lower levels allows for even washing 8. Equipped with a powerful drain motor 9. Upper and lower partial washing selection button function allows you to save water, time, and energy when washing small amounts of dishes Is the cleaning power good? Yes, it is good. It washes well with high temperature washing at 75 degrees and 3-stage three-dimensional water flow. These days, the performance of dishwashers is similar or not much different, and the most important factor is that the detergent is responsible for 90%, so refer to Coupang reviews and wash with an all-in-one detergent containing a rinse ingredient. It washes well, has less water droplets after washing, dries quickly, and has less water stains. For reference, I used Nellie powder detergent without a rinse ingredient, and it had a lot of water droplets, had quite a few water stains, and didn't smell good, but the residual detergent remains due to the rinse, so if you have infants or children, it is recommended to avoid using rinse. I have a very sensitive constitution, so I bought a detergent without a rinse ingredient, and I am willing to accept the disadvantages. Overall review: It is a cost-effective media product that has almost all the advanced functions of expensive products from large domestic companies, but is half the price. Buy it quickly and get out of the dishwashing hell as soon as possible. It is a new world. However, it is good to pay a certain amount of money for domestic products and use regular care services or receive after-sales service. There are advantages, but since this product is made in China, there may be inconveniences in receiving quick service. I hope you will make a good choice by keeping that in mind and ending my review.

People who have a healthy back but are neat and cannot stand seeing dishes pile up and want to wash the dishes right away. People who do not have space to install a 12-person one due to a small kitchen. 2) Who should buy a 12-person one? . A household with a family of 4 or more, where there is a lot of dishes to wash every day, or even a family of 2, who has a laid-back personality and is easygoing enough to wash a lot of dishes at once without it being an eyesore. Buy it quickly and get out of the dishwashing hell as soon as possible. It is a new world. However, it is good to pay a certain amount of money for domestic products and use regular care services or receive after-sales service. There are advantages, but since this product is made in China, there may be inconveniences in receiving quick service. I hope you will make a good choice by keeping that in mind and ending my review.

People who have a healthy back but are neat and cannot stand seeing dishes pile up and want to wash the dishes right away. People who do not have space to install a 12-person one due to a small kitchen. 2) Who should buy a 12-person one? . A household with a family of 4 or more, where there is a lot of dishes to wash every day, or even a family of 2, who has a laid-back personality and is easygoing enough to wash a lot of dishes at once without it being an eyesore. I have a very sensitive constitution, so I bought a detergent without a rinse ingredient, and I am willing to accept the disadvantages. Overall review: It is a cost-effective media product that has almost all the advanced functions of expensive products from large domestic companies, but is half the price. Buy it quickly and get out of the dishwashing hell as soon as possible. It is a new world. However, it is good to pay a certain amount of money for domestic products and use regular care services or receive after-sales service. There are advantages, but since this product is made in China, there may be inconveniences in receiving quick service. I hope you will make a good choice by keeping that in mind and ending my review.

Sentence (English): I put it up right next to the kitchen, so I turn it on after breakfast, and I turn it on after dinner.

It is very useful because it is a house where pots and pans are not washed every time, and bowls for rice, soup, and side dishes and snacks are often served. It has an automatic door opening function, so you can turn it back in the morning when dropping off your child and have clean dishes again when you get home from work. I don't like having a lot of water in the sink, but it makes cleaning the kitchen much easier because I don't have to splash water every time I wash the dishes. I recommend it to families of 1 to 3 people, and the cleaning power is also better than what I washed myself. There was a menu called low-temperature washing, so I cleaned dishes and cups with pretty prints that I was worried about getting damaged, but they were fine when I washed them with low-temperature washing. On the other hand, if you wash greasy tongs and scissors (after grilling meat) at high temperature, they become nice and crispy. I can hear the sound since I place it on the sink, but it's not enough to bother me. I was worried about what would happen if the exterior material got dirty or stained every time it came into contact with water, but not at all. Even though I drip it every time, it doesn't leave a trace. The dishwashing time is short, about 60 minutes, and it is easily accessible, so I end up doing it often, and the time I spent worrying about whether to buy it or not is in vain ^^;. +) I previously used a product for 12 to 14 people, but the cleaning power was disappointing, and a lot of water was spilled during the process of moving it from the sink to the dishwasher, so I had to wipe the floor, which was a hassle. Also, it was a hassle to remove dishes after using the dishwasher, but the 6-person product has a huge advantage in that you don't have to bend your back. +) Installation was done neatly without any additional holes.
Comments (Original): [ 주방 바로 옆에 올리니까 아침먹고 돌리고, 저녁먹고 돌리고 바로바로 돌립니다.매번 냄비, 후라이팬 설거지나오지 않고, 밥&국그릇, 반찬 간식 담았던 그릇이 자주자주 나오는 ] || ---------------- || 주방 바로 옆에 올리니까 아침먹고 돌리고, 저녁먹고 돌리고 바로바로 돌립니다.매번 냄비, 후라이팬 설거지나오지 않고, 밥&국그릇, 반찬 간식 담았던 그릇이 자주자주 나오는 집이어서 그런지 활용도가 엄청 좋아요.자동 문열림 기능있어서 아침에 아이 데려다주면서 돌려놓고 퇴근하면 다시 또 깨끗한 식기 사용가능하구요.싱크대에 물기많은거 싫어하는데 매번 물튀기면서 설거지안해도 되니 주방청소도 한결 수월합니다.1~3인 가족에게 추천드리고, 세정력 또한 제가 씻은것보다 깨끗하게 되요저온세척이라는 메뉴가 있어서 혹시나 망가질까 염려되었던 그릇이나 프린팅이 예쁜 컵 같은것들은 저온세척으로 세정했는데 멀쩡했구요.반대로 기름기 많은 집게와 가위(고기굽고 난 후)는 고온으로 세척하니 뽀득하게 잘되네요소리는 아무래도 싱크대 위에 올려놓으니 들리긴 하는데, 신경쓰이는 정도는 아니구요.외관 재질이 손때묻거나 물 닿을때마다 얼룩지면 어떡하나 걱정했는데 전혀요. 매번 물뚝뚝흘리는데도 물자국 안남네요. 설거지시간도 60여분정도로 짧고 접근성이 좋으니까 자주자주 돌리게되고 살까말까 고민했던 시간이 무색합니다^^;+) 이전에 12~14인용 제품을 썼었는데 세정력이 아쉬웠고, 싱크대에서 식세기까지 옮기는 과정에서 물을 많이 흘려서 바닥을 닦아줘야하는 번거로움이 있었어요. 또 식세기 작동후에 그릇빼는것이 귀찮았는데, 6인용 제품은 허리를 굽히지 않아도 되는것이 아주 큰 장점입니다.+) 별도의 타공없이 설치도 깔끔하게 잘 되었어요

(I only wish this model had the light indicator on the floor; it's that quiet! ) As with past Bosch dishwashers, I often use the adjustable rack for oversized pans, and the top silverware rack is wonderful too for small things like jar lids and dipping dishes. Moveable silverware baskets and adjustable dish racks top of the list of flexible features that get a good workout in my house. My last Bosch had more options for cycles, but I found I never used most of them, so this time, I chose this model, which is perfect for us. Highly recommended.

Sentence (English): Very easy dishwasher installation.
Comments (English): [ Efficiency and ergonomics ] || ---------------- || Very easy dishwasher installation. We appreciate the ease of daily use, the ergonomics of the storage, the light inside (a very useful gadget when you put away your dishwasher in the evening), and the connection to the smart phone via Home Connect. In terms of performance, nothing to say, the dishes come out perfectly clean and the drying is often perfect (even if it can happen that there is a little water remaining in cups with a rounded bottom). We highly recommend this item.
Comments (Original): [ Efficacité et ergonomie ] || ---------------- || Installation du lave-vaisselle très facile. Nous apprécions la facilité d'utilisation au quotidien, l'ergonomie des rangements, la lumière à l'intérieure (un gadget bien utile quand on range son lave-vaisselle le soir), et la connection au smart phone via Home Connect. Niveau performances, rien à dire, la vaisselle ressort parfaitement propre et le séchage est souvent parfait (même s'il peut arriver qu'il reste un peu d'eau dans des tasses à fond arrondit). Nous recommandons grandement cet article.

Sentence (English): This is an honest review after using several dishwashers.
Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is an honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person one. Of course, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person one. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful detergent. And the Chefborn? I also used a 6-person dishwasher without installation, but what the heck. All the dishes fall under it. You have to make it tight, horizontally and vertically to even fit small dishes. There are just long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are too big, so rice bowls fall out. I only need to put in large dishes, but there's no space for them. If I put a large dish in, it covers the detergent drawer door, preventing it from coming out, or it pops out and keeps the door closed. Seriously. I wondered why they made it this way. In the end, I couldn't use it, so I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher. Then I found this product on Media, and it seems to be exactly the same as the Cuckoo. The product size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo, but Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and has 2 years of after-sales service for rocket installation. Cuckoo is about 250,000 won, and it's a little better if you connect to a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard that the phone doesn't connect at all), but it's a 1:1 chat consultation, so you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. Also, the after-sales service is 1 year, but if you verify something on the official website, it's 1 year and 6 months? It's also difficult to call an installer every time. So in the end, I decided not to use Cuckoo and bought Media. The advantage? It's cheap. The disadvantage? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have an upper nozzle, so it cleans less. I put the frying pan and pot in and spin it. (That's how I've been using the dishwasher so far.) But since the water doesn't come out from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned well and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. The detergent is based on Frosh baking soda. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, put 1/2 to 1/3. You don't need to put all of it. One Frosh is enough for 12 people and half a bottle is enough for 6 people. If you put too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but the smell is strong and I can't cut it, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that would never come off no matter how hard I scrubbed it disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin it after eating fish. There's no need to pre-wash the fatty pork belly. The dishwasher washes 80% with detergent.) The good thing is There's no separate place to insert the cutlery holder, so you can move it to the innermost, outermost, middle, or wherever you want. (The Chef Bon has a fixed place to insert it, which was really inconvenient.) If you put a frying pan or pot on the left, the dishes in the upper left compartment don't get cleaned well, so you might have to move it to the right or left. I think you'll have to get good at Tetris. The cleaning power of all dishwashers is similar anyway, and the detergent makes a difference, but the lack of an upper nozzle definitely makes a difference in cleaning power. Still, if it's your first time using it, you won't feel any problems at all. The inside gets cleaned very well. (It's a detergent wash anyway.) And those who run it right away probably won't feel much of a problem. Those who put it in the basket and run it with oil all over the dishes, or those who downgrade like me, might say, "Hmm." The only thing I mean is that the outside isn't very clean to the touch, but it doesn't feel like the dishes aren't washed well. It's bound to get cleaned better than by hand anyway. Well. I don't know if this media dishwasher will clean very well if you use Cascade, but I can forgive it because it's cheap. The Chefborn fan noise was really annoying after it was done (the fan would run automatically for 72 hours, so even if I opened the door and turned off the power;; If you turn off the ventilation mode, the fan would run even if you turned off the power, but after it was done, the fan would always run, so I had to press the power button to turn it off, which was inconvenient). It's actually nice that there's no such thing, and since I don't need the automatic door opening function, I usually leave the door open right after it's done to dry (the dishes will dry very quickly because they're hot if you shake off the standing water once). I'm not planning to use it for a long time, so I'm using it with satisfaction. If you plan to use it for a long time, it would be better if the water stream came out from the top. Of course, it would be more expensive, but considering the price, this one isn't bad. If you spend more money on detergent, it'll probably cover it to some extent. And the thing that goes in is... It fits as much as the basket is full. I only use frying pans, pots, and tall dishes, so it doesn't feel like it's full. If you use a lot of flat dishes, it seems like it would really fit a lot. Even if you put in just two large frying pans and pots, it's more than half full. (There's a cutlery holder and a little space in front of the detergent dispenser for dishes) It definitely fits less than 12 people. Two people eat three meals a day at home, but they rotate the meals once a day. That's because they eat plain rice and don't eat side dishes. When using it for 12 people, I soaked it in water and turned it once every three days. It doesn't seem to matter how many people live in a household or how many meals we eat a day. Since the size and number of dishes used in each household are different, roughly calculate how much dishware will be produced and then purchase it. Also, I use thick chopsticks sold at Daiso for the stir-fry so they don't fall out easily. I use Magic Hands? handles that can be attached and detached for both the frying pan and the pot, so I can load large frying pans and pots without any inconvenience. (Tefal is expensive, so I've been using the cheaper Magic Hands product. I've had it for over a year and the coating doesn't come off no matter how hard I spin the dishwasher, so it's great.) The drilling holes are 6mm. The installer was very friendly and installed it very quickly. Also, when I used the Chefborn 6-person installation-free dishwasher, I bought a 20L water tank and filled it with it. Since I don't find that very inconvenient, I asked if I could use it in a water tank to avoid drilling, but the technician said that it was not possible. If it were possible, I would have sold it as an installation-free dishwasher, right? Non-installed dishwashers are supposed to have a water-sucking function, but this one should automatically have water coming in. If you have a water purifier, you can connect it there, but since I don't have a water purifier, I drilled a hole in the marble countertop where it's not visible and connected it under the sink. When I asked about dismantling it later, they kindly explained it to me. Sentence (English): I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person one.
Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is an honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person one. Of course, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person one. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful detergent. And the Chefborn? I also used a 6-person dishwasher without installation, but what the heck. All the dishes fall under it. You have to make it tight, horizontally and vertically to even fit small dishes. There are just long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are too big, so rice bowls fall out. I only need to put in large dishes, but there's no space for them. If I put a large dish in, it covers the detergent drawer door, preventing it from coming out, or it pops out and keeps the door closed. Seriously. I wondered why they made it this way. In the end, I couldn't use it, so I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher. Then I found this product on Media, and it seems to be exactly the same as the Cuckoo. The product size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo, but Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and has 2 years of after-sales service for rocket installation. Cuckoo is about 250,000 won, and it's a little better if you connect to a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard that the phone doesn't connect at all), but it's a 1:1 chat consultation, so you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. Also, the after-sales service is 1 year, but if you verify something on the official website, it's 1 year and 6 months? It's also difficult to call an installer every time. So in the end, I decided not to use Cuckoo and bought Media. The advantage? It's cheap. The disadvantage? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have an upper nozzle, so it cleans less. I put the frying pan and pot in and spin it. (That's how I've been using the dishwasher so far.) But since the water doesn't come out from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned well and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. The detergent is based on Frosh baking soda. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, put 1/2 to 1/3. You don't need to put all of it. One Frosh is enough for 12 people and half a bottle is enough for 6 people. If you put too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but the smell is strong and I can't cut it, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and price, use Cascade Platinum. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is an honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person one. Of course, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person one. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful detergent. And the Chefborn? I also used a 6-person dishwasher without installation, but what the heck. All the dishes fall under it. You have to make it tight, horizontally and vertically to even fit small dishes. There are just long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are too big, so rice bowls fall out. I only need to put in large dishes, but there's no space for them. If I put a large dish in, it covers the detergent drawer door, preventing it from coming out, or it pops out and keeps the door closed. Seriously. I wondered why they made it this way. In the end, I couldn't use it, so I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher. Then I found this product on Media, and it seems to be exactly the same as the Cuckoo. The product size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo, but Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and has 2 years of after-sales service for rocket installation. Cuckoo is about 250,000 won, and it's a little better if you connect to a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard that the phone doesn't connect at all), but it's a 1:1 chat consultation, so you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. Also, the after-sales service is 1 year, but if you verify something on the official website, it's 1 year and 6 months? It's also difficult to call an installer every time. So in the end, I decided not to use Cuckoo and bought Media. The advantage? It's cheap. The disadvantage? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have an upper nozzle, so it cleans less. I put the frying pan and pot in and spin it. (That's how I've been using the dishwasher so far.) But since the water doesn't come out from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned well and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. The detergent is based on Frosh baking soda. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, put 1/2 to 1/3. You don't need to put all of it. One Frosh is enough for 12 people and half a bottle is enough for 6 people. If you put too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but the smell is strong and I can't cut it, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that would never come off no matter how hard I scrubbed it disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin it after eating fish. There's no need to pre-wash the fatty pork belly. The dishwasher washes 80% with detergent.) The good thing is There's no separate place to insert the cutlery holder, so you can move it to the innermost, outermost, middle, or wherever you want. (The Chef Bon has a fixed place to insert it, which was really inconvenient.) If you put a frying pan or pot on the left, the dishes in the upper left compartment don't get cleaned well, so you might have to move it to the right or left. I think you'll have to get good at Tetris. The cleaning power of all dishwashers is similar anyway, and the detergent makes a difference, but the lack of an upper nozzle definitely makes a difference in cleaning power. Still, if it's your first time using it, you won't feel any problems at all. The inside gets cleaned very well. (It's a detergent wash anyway.) And those who run it right away probably won't feel much of a problem. Those who put it in the basket and run it with oil all over the dishes, or those who downgrade like me, might say, "Hmm." The only thing I mean is that the outside isn't very clean to the touch, but it doesn't feel like the dishes aren't washed well. It's bound to get cleaned better than by hand anyway. Well. I don't know if this media dishwasher will clean very well if you use Cascade, but I can forgive it because it's cheap. The Chefborn fan noise was really annoying after it was done (the fan would run automatically for 72 hours, so even if I opened the door and turned off the power;; If you turn off the ventilation mode, the fan would run even if you turned off the power, but after it was done, the fan would always run, so I had to press the power button to turn it off, which was inconvenient). It's actually nice that there's no such thing, and since I don't need the automatic door opening function, I usually leave the door open right after it's done to dry (the dishes will dry very quickly because they're hot if you shake off the standing water once). I'm not planning to use it for a long time, so I'm using it with satisfaction. If you plan to use it for a long time, it would be better if the water stream came out from the top. Of course, it would be more expensive, but considering the price, this one isn't bad. If you spend more money on detergent, it'll probably cover it to some extent. And the thing that goes in is... It fits as much as the basket is full. I only use frying pans, pots, and tall dishes, so it doesn't feel like it's full. If you use a lot of flat dishes, it seems like it would really fit a lot. Even if you put in just two large frying pans and pots, it's more than half full. (There's a cutlery holder and a little space in front of the detergent dispenser for dishes) It definitely fits less than 12 people. Two people eat three meals a day at home, but they rotate the meals once a day. That's because they eat plain rice and don't eat side dishes. When using it for 12 people, I soaked it in water and turned it once every three days. It doesn't seem to matter how many people live in a household or how many meals we eat a day. Since the size and number of dishes used in each household are different, roughly calculate how much dishware will be produced and then purchase it. Also, I use thick chopsticks sold at Daiso for the stir-fry so they don't fall out easily. I use Magic Hands? handles that can be attached and detached for both the frying pan and the pot, so I can load large frying pans and pots without any inconvenience. (Tefal is expensive, so I've been using the cheaper Magic Hands product. I've had it for over a year and the coating doesn't come off no matter how hard I spin the dishwasher, so it's great.) The drilling holes are 6mm. The installer was very friendly and installed it very quickly. Also, when I used the Chefborn 6-person installation-free dishwasher, I bought a 20L water tank and filled it with it. Since I don't find that very inconvenient, I asked if I could use it in a water tank to avoid drilling, but the technician said that it was not possible. If it were possible, I would have sold it as an installation-free dishwasher, right? Non-installed dishwashers are supposed to have a water-sucking function, but this one should automatically have water coming in. If you have a water purifier, you can connect it there, but since I don't have a water purifier, I drilled a hole in the marble countertop where it's not visible and connected it under the sink. When I asked about dismantling it later, they kindly explained it to me. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher. Naturally, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person dishwasher. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? Everything falls under the dishes. You have to place them tightly, horizontally and vertically, to even fit small dishes. Seriously, there are just long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are so big that rice bowls fall through. I'm only supposed to put in large dishes, but there's no room for them. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. I can't cut it up, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and the price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that would never come off no matter how hard I scrubbed will disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin the fish you ate. You don't need to pre-wash the fatty pork belly. 80% of dishwashers are detergent-washed.) The good thing is that there's no separate place to insert the cutlery holder, so you can move it to the innermost, outermost, middle, or wherever you want. (The Cheffubon had a fixed place to insert it, so it was really inconvenient.) If you put a frying pan or pot on the left, the dishes on the upper left shelf won't clean well. Or maybe you should move it to the right. I think you need to play Tetris a little better. Dishwashers all have similar cleaning power, and the detergent makes a difference. The lack of a top nozzle definitely makes a difference in cleaning power. Still, if you're a first-time user, you probably won't notice any issues. The inside gets cleaned really well (since it's detergent-washing anyway). And those who just start the cycle won't feel much of a problem. You can put the dishes in the basket and run them while they're all oily. Those who downgrade like me might say, "Hmm." It's just that the outside isn't quite as clean when you touch it. It doesn't mean they're not washed well. They're bound to get better than hand washing anyway. Well, I'm not sure if this media dishwasher with a cascade function will clean them very well. I forgive it because it's cheap. The fan noise from the Chefborn was really annoying afterward. (The fan would run automatically for 72 hours, so even if I opened the door and turned off the power, the fan would run;; If I turned off the ventilation mode, the fan would stop running even if I turned off the power, but after I finished, the fan would always run, so I had to press the power button to turn it off, which was inconvenient.) It's actually nice that there's no such thing. I don't need the automatic door opening function. After I'm done, I usually leave the door open to dry it. (If you shake off any standing water, the dishes will dry very quickly because they're hot.) I'm not planning on using it for a long time, so I'm satisfied with it. For those who plan on using it for a long time, it would be better if the water stream came out from the top. Of course, it would be more expensive. Considering the price, this one isn't bad. I think spending more money on detergent would cover it to some extent. And it holds. It holds as much as the basket size. I only use frying pans, pots, and tall dishes, so it doesn't feel like it's full. If you use a lot of flat dishes, it seems like it would really hold a lot. Even if I put in just two large frying pans and pots, it's more than half full. (There's a cutlery holder and a little space in front of the detergent dispenser for dishes). It definitely holds less than a 12-person dishwasher. Two people eat three meals a day at home, so we only turn it once a day. We eat rice and don't eat side dishes, so that's understandable. When using a 12-person dishwasher, we soaked it in water and turned it once every three days. It doesn't seem to matter how many people live in a household or how many meals a day they eat. Each household uses different sizes and quantities of dishes, so roughly estimate how much you'll need before purchasing. I use the thick chopsticks sold at Daiso for the stirrers, so they don't fall out easily. For both the frying pan and pot, I use Magic Hands, which have detachable handles. The installer was very friendly and installed quickly. Sentence (English): I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher. Naturally, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person dishwasher. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? Everything falls under the dishes. You have to place them tightly, horizontally and vertically, to even fit small dishes. Seriously, there are just long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are so big that rice bowls fall through. I'm only supposed to put in large dishes, but there's no room for them. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. I can't cut it up, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and the price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that would never come off no matter how hard I scrubbed will disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin the fish you ate. You don't need to pre-wash the fatty pork belly. 80% of dishwashers are detergent-washed.) The good thing is that there's no separate place to insert the cutlery holder, so you can move it to the innermost, outermost, middle, or wherever you want. (The Cheffubon had a fixed place to insert it, so it was really inconvenient.) If you put a frying pan or pot on the left, the dishes on the upper left shelf won't clean well. Or maybe you should move it to the right. I think you need to play Tetris a little better. Dishwashers all have similar cleaning power, and the detergent makes a difference. The lack of a top nozzle definitely makes a difference in cleaning power. Still, if you're a first-time user, you probably won't notice any issues. The inside gets cleaned really well (since it's detergent-washing anyway). And those who just start the cycle won't feel much of a problem. You can put the dishes in the basket and run them while they're all oily. Those who downgrade like me might say, "Hmm." It's just that the outside isn't quite as clean when you touch it. It doesn't mean they're not washed well. They're bound to get better than hand washing anyway. Well, I'm not sure if this media dishwasher with a cascade function will clean them very well. I forgive it because it's cheap. The fan noise from the Chefborn was really annoying afterward. (The fan would run automatically for 72 hours, so even if I opened the door and turned off the power, the fan would run;; If I turned off the ventilation mode, the fan would stop running even if I turned off the power, but after I finished, the fan would always run, so I had to press the power button to turn it off, which was inconvenient.) It's actually nice that there's no such thing. I don't need the automatic door opening function. After I'm done, I usually leave the door open to dry it. (If you shake off any standing water, the dishes will dry very quickly because they're hot.) I'm not planning on using it for a long time, so I'm satisfied with it. For those who plan on using it for a long time, it would be better if the water stream came out from the top. Of course, it would be more expensive. Considering the price, this one isn't bad. I think spending more money on detergent would cover it to some extent. And it holds. It holds as much as the basket size. I only use frying pans, pots, and tall dishes, so it doesn't feel like it's full. If you use a lot of flat dishes, it seems like it would really hold a lot. Even if I put in just two large frying pans and pots, it's more than half full. (There's a cutlery holder and a little space in front of the detergent dispenser for dishes). It definitely holds less than a 12-person dishwasher. Two people eat three meals a day at home, so we only turn it once a day. We eat rice and don't eat side dishes, so that's understandable. When using a 12-person dishwasher, we soaked it in water and turned it once every three days. It doesn't seem to matter how many people live in a household or how many meals a day they eat. Each household uses different sizes and quantities of dishes, so roughly estimate how much you'll need before purchasing. I use the thick chopsticks sold at Daiso for the stirrers, so they don't fall out easily. For both the frying pan and pot, I use Magic Hands, which have detachable handles. I can load large frying pans and pots without any problems. (Tefal is expensive, so I've been using the cheaper Magic Hands. I've had them for over a year, and they're great because the coating doesn't peel off even when I run the dishwasher hard.) The drilled holes are 6mm. The installer was very friendly and installed quickly. When I used the Chefbone 6-seater, no-installation dishwasher, I used to fill it with a 20-liter water tank, and since I didn't find that particularly inconvenient, I asked if I could use a water tank to avoid drilling holes. The technician said it wasn't possible. If it were possible, they would have sold it as a no-installation dishwasher, right? No-installation dishwashers have a water-sucking function. This one should automatically draw water in. If you have a water purifier, you can connect it there. I don't have a water purifier, so I drilled a hole in the marble countertop where it's not easily visible and connected it under the sink. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? And the holes in the front are so big that rice bowls fall through. I'm only supposed to put in large dishes, but there's no room for them. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? And the holes in the front are so big that rice bowls fall through. I'm only supposed to put in large dishes, but there's no room for them. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher. Naturally, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person dishwasher. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? Everything falls under the dishes. You have to place them tightly, horizontally and vertically, to even fit small dishes. Seriously, there are just long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are so big that rice bowls fall through. I'm only supposed to put in large dishes, but there's no room for them. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. I can't cut it up, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and the price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that would never come off no matter how hard I scrubbed will disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin the fish you ate. You don't need to pre-wash the fatty pork belly. 80% of dishwashers are detergent-washed.) The good thing is that there's no separate place to insert the cutlery holder, so you can move it to the innermost, outermost, middle, or wherever you want. (The Cheffubon had a fixed place to insert it, so it was really inconvenient.) If you put a frying pan or pot on the left, the dishes on the upper left shelf won't clean well. Or maybe you should move it to the right. I think you need to play Tetris a little better. Dishwashers all have similar cleaning power, and the detergent makes a difference. The lack of a top nozzle definitely makes a difference in cleaning power. Still, if you're a first-time user, you probably won't notice any issues. The inside gets cleaned really well (since it's detergent-washing anyway). And those who just start the cycle won't feel much of a problem. You can put the dishes in the basket and run them while they're all oily. Those who downgrade like me might say, "Hmm." It's just that the outside isn't quite as clean when you touch it. It doesn't mean they're not washed well. They're bound to get better than hand washing anyway. Well, I'm not sure if this media dishwasher with a cascade function will clean them very well. I forgive it because it's cheap. The fan noise from the Chefborn was really annoying afterward. (The fan would run automatically for 72 hours, so even if I opened the door and turned off the power, the fan would run;; If I turned off the ventilation mode, the fan would stop running even if I turned off the power, but after I finished, the fan would always run, so I had to press the power button to turn it off, which was inconvenient.) It's actually nice that there's no such thing. I don't need the automatic door opening function. After I'm done, I usually leave the door open to dry it. (If you shake off any standing water, the dishes will dry very quickly because they're hot.) I'm not planning on using it for a long time, so I'm satisfied with it. For those who plan on using it for a long time, it would be better if the water stream came out from the top. Of course, it would be more expensive. Considering the price, this one isn't bad. I think spending more money on detergent would cover it to some extent. And it holds. It holds as much as the basket size. I only use frying pans, pots, and tall dishes, so it doesn't feel like it's full. If you use a lot of flat dishes, it seems like it would really hold a lot. Even if I put in just two large frying pans and pots, it's more than half full. (There's a cutlery holder and a little space in front of the detergent dispenser for dishes). It definitely holds less than a 12-person dishwasher. Two people eat three meals a day at home, so we only turn it once a day. We eat rice and don't eat side dishes, so that's understandable. When using a 12-person dishwasher, we soaked it in water and turned it once every three days. It doesn't seem to matter how many people live in a household or how many meals a day they eat. Each household uses different sizes and quantities of dishes, so roughly estimate how much you'll need before purchasing. I use the thick chopsticks sold at Daiso for the stirrers, so they don't fall out easily. For both the frying pan and pot, I use Magic Hands, which have detachable handles. I can load large frying pans and pots without any problems. (Tefal is expensive, so I've been using the cheaper Magic Hands. The installer was very friendly and installed quickly. Sentence (English): I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher. Naturally, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person dishwasher. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? Everything falls under the dishes. You have to place them tightly, horizontally and vertically, to even fit small dishes. Seriously, there are just long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are so big that rice bowls fall through. I'm only supposed to put in large dishes, but there's no room for them. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. I can't cut it up, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and the price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that would never come off no matter how hard I scrubbed will disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin the fish you ate. You don't need to pre-wash the fatty pork belly. 80% of dishwashers are detergent-washed.) The good thing is that there's no separate place to insert the cutlery holder, so you can move it to the innermost, outermost, middle, or wherever you want. (The Cheffubon had a fixed place to insert it, so it was really inconvenient.) If you put a frying pan or pot on the left, the dishes on the upper left shelf won't clean well. Or maybe you should move it to the right. I think you need to play Tetris a little better. Dishwashers all have similar cleaning power, and the detergent makes a difference. The lack of a top nozzle definitely makes a difference in cleaning power. Still, if you're a first-time user, you probably won't notice any issues. The inside gets cleaned really well (since it's detergent-washing anyway). And those who just start the cycle won't feel much of a problem. You can put the dishes in the basket and run them while they're all oily. Those who downgrade like me might say, "Hmm." It's just that the outside isn't quite as clean when you touch it. It doesn't mean they're not washed well. They're bound to get better than hand washing anyway. Well, I'm not sure if this media dishwasher with a cascade function will clean them very well. I forgive it because it's cheap. The fan noise from the Chefborn was really annoying afterward. (The fan would run automatically for 72 hours, so even if I opened the door and turned off the power, the fan would run;; If I turned off the ventilation mode, the fan would stop running even if I turned off the power, but after I finished, the fan would always run, so I had to press the power button to turn it off, which was inconvenient.) It's actually nice that there's no such thing. I don't need the automatic door opening function. After I'm done, I usually leave the door open to dry it. (If you shake off any standing water, the dishes will dry very quickly because they're hot.) I'm not planning on using it for a long time, so I'm satisfied with it. For those who plan on using it for a long time, it would be better if the water stream came out from the top. Of course, it would be more expensive. Considering the price, this one isn't bad. I think spending more money on detergent would cover it to some extent. And it holds. It holds as much as the basket size. I only use frying pans, pots, and tall dishes, so it doesn't feel like it's full. If you use a lot of flat dishes, it seems like it would really hold a lot. Even if I put in just two large frying pans and pots, it's more than half full. (There's a cutlery holder and a little space in front of the detergent dispenser for dishes). It definitely holds less than a 12-person dishwasher. Two people eat three meals a day at home, so we only turn it once a day. We eat rice and don't eat side dishes, so that's understandable. When using a 12-person dishwasher, we soaked it in water and turned it once every three days. It doesn't seem to matter how many people live in a household or how many meals a day they eat. Each household uses different sizes and quantities of dishes, so roughly estimate how much you'll need before purchasing. I use the thick chopsticks sold at Daiso for the stirrers, so they don't fall out easily. For both the frying pan and pot, I use Magic Hands, which have detachable handles. I can load large frying pans and pots without any problems. (Tefal is expensive, so I've been using the cheaper Magic Hands. I've had them for over a year, and they're great because the coating doesn't peel off even when I run the dishwasher hard.) The drilled holes are 6mm. The installer was very friendly and installed quickly. When I used the Chefbone 6-seater, no-installation dishwasher, I used to fill it with a 20-liter water tank, and since I didn't find that particularly inconvenient, I asked if I could use a water tank to avoid drilling holes. The technician said it wasn't possible. If it were possible, they would have sold it as a no-installation dishwasher, right? No-installation dishwashers have a water-sucking function. This one should automatically draw water in. If you have a water purifier, you can connect it there. I don't have a water purifier, so I drilled a hole in the marble countertop where it's not easily visible and connected it under the sink. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher. Naturally, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person dishwasher. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher. Naturally, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person dishwasher. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? Everything falls under the dishes. You have to place them tightly, horizontally and vertically, to even fit small dishes. Seriously, there are just long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are so big that rice bowls fall through. I'm only supposed to put in large dishes, but there's no room for them. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. I can't cut it up, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and the price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that would never come off no matter how hard I scrubbed will disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin the fish you ate. You don't need to pre-wash the fatty pork belly. 80% of dishwashers are detergent-washed.) I forgive it because it's cheap. The fan noise from the Chefborn was really annoying afterward. (The fan would run automatically for 72 hours, so even if I opened the door and turned off the power, the fan would run;; If I turned off the ventilation mode, the fan would stop running even if I turned off the power, but after I finished, the fan would always run, so I had to press the power button to turn it off, which was inconvenient.) It's actually nice that there's no such thing. I don't need the automatic door opening function. After I'm done, I usually leave the door open to dry it. (If you shake off any standing water, the dishes will dry very quickly because they're hot.) I'm not planning on using it for a long time, so I'm satisfied with it. For those who plan on using it for a long time, it would be better if the water stream came out from the top. Of course, it would be more expensive. Considering the price, this one isn't bad. I think spending more money on detergent would cover it to some extent. And it holds. It holds as much as the basket size. Sentence (English): I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo.
Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher. Naturally, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person dishwasher. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? Everything falls under the dishes. You have to place them tightly, horizontally and vertically, to even fit small dishes. Seriously, there are just long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are so big that rice bowls fall through. I'm only supposed to put in large dishes, but there's no room for them. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. I can't cut it up, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and the price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that would never come off no matter how hard I scrubbed will disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin the fish you ate. You don't need to pre-wash the fatty pork belly. 80% of dishwashers are detergent-washed.) The good thing is that there's no separate place to insert the cutlery holder, so you can move it to the innermost, outermost, middle, or wherever you want. (The Cheffubon had a fixed place to insert it, so it was really inconvenient.) If you put a frying pan or pot on the left, the dishes on the upper left shelf won't clean well. Or maybe you should move it to the right. I think you need to play Tetris a little better. Dishwashers all have similar cleaning power, and the detergent makes a difference. The lack of a top nozzle definitely makes a difference in cleaning power. Still, if you're a first-time user, you probably won't notice any issues. The inside gets cleaned really well (since it's detergent-washing anyway). And those who just start the cycle won't feel much of a problem. You can put the dishes in the basket and run them while they're all oily. Those who downgrade like me might say, "Hmm." It's just that the outside isn't quite as clean when you touch it. It doesn't mean they're not washed well. They're bound to get better than hand washing anyway. Well, I'm not sure if this media dishwasher with a cascade function will clean them very well. I forgive it because it's cheap. The fan noise from the Chefborn was really annoying afterward. (The fan would run automatically for 72 hours, so even if I opened the door and turned off the power, the fan would run;; If I turned off the ventilation mode, the fan would stop running even if I turned off the power, but after I finished, the fan would always run, so I had to press the power button to turn it off, which was inconvenient.) It's actually nice that there's no such thing. I don't need the automatic door opening function. After I'm done, I usually leave the door open to dry it. (If you shake off any standing water, the dishes will dry very quickly because they're hot.) I'm not planning on using it for a long time, so I'm satisfied with it. For those who plan on using it for a long time, it would be better if the water stream came out from the top. Of course, it would be more expensive. Considering the price, this one isn't bad. I think spending more money on detergent would cover it to some extent. And it holds. It holds as much as the basket size. I only use frying pans, pots, and tall dishes, so it doesn't feel like it's full. If you use a lot of flat dishes, it seems like it would really hold a lot. Even if I put in just two large frying pans and pots, it's more than half full. (There's a cutlery holder and a little space in front of the detergent dispenser for dishes). It definitely holds less than a 12-person dishwasher. Two people eat three meals a day at home, so we only turn it once a day. We eat rice and don't eat side dishes, so that's understandable. When using a 12-person dishwasher, we soaked it in water and turned it once every three days. It doesn't seem to matter how many people live in a household or how many meals a day they eat. Each household uses different sizes and quantities of dishes, so roughly estimate how much you'll need before purchasing. I use the thick chopsticks sold at Daiso for the stirrers, so they don't fall out easily. For both the frying pan and pot, I use Magic Hands, which have detachable handles. I can load large frying pans and pots without any problems. (Tefal is expensive, so I've been using the cheaper Magic Hands. I've had them for over a year, and they're great because the coating doesn't peel off even when I run the dishwasher hard.) The drilled holes are 6mm. The installer was very friendly and installed quickly. When I used the Chefbone 6-seater, no-installation dishwasher, I used to fill it with a 20-liter water tank, and since I didn't find that particularly inconvenient, I asked if I could use a water tank to avoid drilling holes. The technician said it wasn't possible. If it were possible, they would have sold it as a no-installation dishwasher, right? No-installation dishwashers have a water-sucking function. This one should automatically draw water in. If you have a water purifier, you can connect it there. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher. Naturally, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person dishwasher. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? Everything falls under the dishes. You have to place them tightly, horizontally and vertically, to even fit small dishes. Seriously, there are just long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are so big that rice bowls fall through. I'm only supposed to put in large dishes, but there's no room for them. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. I can't cut it up, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and the price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that would never come off no matter how hard I scrubbed will disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin the fish you ate. You don't need to pre-wash the fatty pork belly. 80% of dishwashers are detergent-washed.) I forgive it because it's cheap. The fan noise from the Chefborn was really annoying afterward. (The fan would run automatically for 72 hours, so even if I opened the door and turned off the power, the fan would run;; If I turned off the ventilation mode, the fan would stop running even if I turned off the power, but after I finished, the fan would always run, so I had to press the power button to turn it off, which was inconvenient.) It's actually nice that there's no such thing. I don't need the automatic door opening function. After I'm done, I usually leave the door open to dry it. (If you shake off any standing water, the dishes will dry very quickly because they're hot.) I'm not planning on using it for a long time, so I'm satisfied with it. For those who plan on using it for a long time, it would be better if the water stream came out from the top. Of course, it would be more expensive. Considering the price, this one isn't bad. I think spending more money on detergent would cover it to some extent. And it holds. It holds as much as the basket size.
