Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher. Naturally, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person dishwasher. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? Everything falls under the dishes. You have to place them tightly, horizontally and vertically, to even fit small dishes. Seriously, there are just long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are so big that rice bowls fall through. I'm only supposed to put in large dishes, but there's no room for them. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. I can't cut it up, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and the price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that would never come off no matter how hard I scrubbed will disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin the fish you ate. You don't need to pre-wash the fatty pork belly. 80% of dishwashers are detergent-washed.) The good thing is that there's no separate place to insert the cutlery holder, so you can move it to the innermost, outermost, middle, or wherever you want. (The Cheffubon had a fixed place to insert it, so it was really inconvenient.) If you put a frying pan or pot on the left, the dishes on the upper left shelf won't clean well. Or maybe you should move it to the right. I think you need to play Tetris a little better. Dishwashers all have similar cleaning power, and the detergent makes a difference. The lack of a top nozzle definitely makes a difference in cleaning power. Still, if you're a first-time user, you probably won't notice any issues. The inside gets cleaned really well (since it's detergent-washing anyway). And those who just start the cycle won't feel much of a problem. You can put the dishes in the basket and run them while they're all oily. Those who downgrade like me might say, "Hmm." It's just that the outside isn't quite as clean when you touch it. It doesn't mean they're not washed well. They're bound to get better than hand washing anyway. Well, I'm not sure if this media dishwasher with a cascade function will clean them very well. I forgive it because it's cheap. The fan noise from the Chefborn was really annoying afterward. (The fan would run automatically for 72 hours, so even if I opened the door and turned off the power, the fan would run;; If I turned off the ventilation mode, the fan would stop running even if I turned off the power, but after I finished, the fan would always run, so I had to press the power button to turn it off, which was inconvenient.) It's actually nice that there's no such thing. I don't need the automatic door opening function. After I'm done, I usually leave the door open to dry it. (If you shake off any standing water, the dishes will dry very quickly because they're hot.) I'm not planning on using it for a long time, so I'm satisfied with it. For those who plan on using it for a long time, it would be better if the water stream came out from the top. Of course, it would be more expensive. Considering the price, this one isn't bad. I think spending more money on detergent would cover it to some extent. And it holds. It holds as much as the basket size. I only use frying pans, pots, and tall dishes, so it doesn't feel like it's full. If you use a lot of flat dishes, it seems like it would really hold a lot. It definitely holds less than a 12-person dishwasher. Two people eat three meals a day at home, so we only turn it once a day. We eat rice and don't eat side dishes, so that's understandable. When using a 12-person dishwasher, we soaked it in water and turned it once every three days. It doesn't seem to matter how many people live in a household or how many meals a day they eat. Each household uses different sizes and quantities of dishes, so roughly estimate how much you'll need before purchasing. I use the thick chopsticks sold at Daiso for the stirrers, so they don't fall out easily. For both the frying pan and pot, I use Magic Hands, which have detachable handles. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher. Naturally, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person dishwasher. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? Everything falls under the dishes. You have to place them tightly, horizontally and vertically, to even fit small dishes. Seriously, there are just long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are so big that rice bowls fall through. I'm only supposed to put in large dishes, but there's no room for them. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. I can't cut it up, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and the price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that would never come off no matter how hard I scrubbed will disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin the fish you ate. You don't need to pre-wash the fatty pork belly. 80% of dishwashers are detergent-washed.) Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. I forgive it because it's cheap. The fan noise from the Chefborn was really annoying afterward. (The fan would run automatically for 72 hours, so even if I opened the door and turned off the power, the fan would run;; If I turned off the ventilation mode, the fan would stop running even if I turned off the power, but after I finished, the fan would always run, so I had to press the power button to turn it off, which was inconvenient.) Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher. Naturally, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person dishwasher. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? Everything falls under the dishes. You have to place them tightly, horizontally and vertically, to even fit small dishes. Seriously, there are just long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are so big that rice bowls fall through. I'm only supposed to put in large dishes, but there's no room for them. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. I can't cut it up, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and the price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that would never come off no matter how hard I scrubbed will disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin the fish you ate. You don't need to pre-wash the fatty pork belly. 80% of dishwashers are detergent-washed.) The good thing is that there's no separate place to insert the cutlery holder, so you can move it to the innermost, outermost, middle, or wherever you want. The inside gets cleaned really well (since it's detergent-washing anyway). And those who just start the cycle won't feel much of a problem. You can put the dishes in the basket and run them while they're all oily. Those who downgrade like me might say, "Hmm." It's just that the outside isn't quite as clean when you touch it. It doesn't mean they're not washed well. They're bound to get better than hand washing anyway. Well, I'm not sure if this media dishwasher with a cascade function will clean them very well. I forgive it because it's cheap. The fan noise from the Chefborn was really annoying afterward. (The fan would run automatically for 72 hours, so even if I opened the door and turned off the power, the fan would run;; If I turned off the ventilation mode, the fan would stop running even if I turned off the power, but after I finished, the fan would always run, so I had to press the power button to turn it off, which was inconvenient.) It's actually nice that there's no such thing. I don't need the automatic door opening function. After I'm done, I usually leave the door open to dry it. (If you shake off any standing water, the dishes will dry very quickly because they're hot.) I'm not planning on using it for a long time, so I'm satisfied with it. For those who plan on using it for a long time, it would be better if the water stream came out from the top. Of course, it would be more expensive. Considering the price, this one isn't bad. I think spending more money on detergent would cover it to some extent. And it holds. It holds as much as the basket size. I use the thick chopsticks sold at Daiso for the stirrers, so they don't fall out easily. For both the frying pan and pot, I use Magic Hands, which have detachable handles. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher. Naturally, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person dishwasher. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? And the holes in the front are so big that rice bowls fall through. I'm only supposed to put in large dishes, but there's no room for them. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. I can't cut it up, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and the price, use Cascade Platinum. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher. Naturally, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person dishwasher. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher. Naturally, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person dishwasher. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? Everything falls under the dishes. You have to place them tightly, horizontally and vertically, to even fit small dishes. Seriously, there are just long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are so big that rice bowls fall through. I'm only supposed to put in large dishes, but there's no room for them. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. I can't cut it up, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and the price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that would never come off no matter how hard I scrubbed will disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin the fish you ate. You don't need to pre-wash the fatty pork belly. 80% of dishwashers are detergent-washed.) Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher. Naturally, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person dishwasher. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? Everything falls under the dishes. You have to place them tightly, horizontally and vertically, to even fit small dishes. Seriously, there are just long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are so big that rice bowls fall through. I'm only supposed to put in large dishes, but there's no room for them. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. I can't cut it up, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and the price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that would never come off no matter how hard I scrubbed will disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin the fish you ate. You don't need to pre-wash the fatty pork belly. 80% of dishwashers are detergent-washed.) The good thing is that there's no separate place to insert the cutlery holder, so you can move it to the innermost, outermost, middle, or wherever you want. (The Cheffubon had a fixed place to insert it, so it was really inconvenient.) If you put a frying pan or pot on the left, the dishes on the upper left shelf won't clean well. Or maybe you should move it to the right. I think you need to play Tetris a little better. Dishwashers all have similar cleaning power, and the detergent makes a difference. The lack of a top nozzle definitely makes a difference in cleaning power. Still, if you're a first-time user, you probably won't notice any issues. The inside gets cleaned really well (since it's detergent-washing anyway). And those who just start the cycle won't feel much of a problem. You can put the dishes in the basket and run them while they're all oily. Those who downgrade like me might say, "Hmm." It's just that the outside isn't quite as clean when you touch it. It doesn't mean they're not washed well. They're bound to get better than hand washing anyway. Well, I'm not sure if this media dishwasher with a cascade function will clean them very well. I forgive it because it's cheap. The fan noise from the Chefborn was really annoying afterward. (The fan would run automatically for 72 hours, so even if I opened the door and turned off the power, the fan would run;; If I turned off the ventilation mode, the fan would stop running even if I turned off the power, but after I finished, the fan would always run, so I had to press the power button to turn it off, which was inconvenient.) It's actually nice that there's no such thing. I don't need the automatic door opening function. After I'm done, I usually leave the door open to dry it. (If you shake off any standing water, the dishes will dry very quickly because they're hot.) I'm not planning on using it for a long time, so I'm satisfied with it. For those who plan on using it for a long time, it would be better if the water stream came out from the top. Of course, it would be more expensive. Considering the price, this one isn't bad. I think spending more money on detergent would cover it to some extent. And it holds. It holds as much as the basket size. I only use frying pans, pots, and tall dishes, so it doesn't feel like it's full. If you use a lot of flat dishes, it seems like it would really hold a lot. Even if I put in just two large frying pans and pots, it's more than half full. (There's a cutlery holder and a little space in front of the detergent dispenser for dishes). It definitely holds less than a 12-person dishwasher. Two people eat three meals a day at home, so we only turn it once a day. We eat rice and don't eat side dishes, so that's understandable. When using a 12-person dishwasher, we soaked it in water and turned it once every three days. It doesn't seem to matter how many people live in a household or how many meals a day they eat. Each household uses different sizes and quantities of dishes, so roughly estimate how much you'll need before purchasing. I use the thick chopsticks sold at Daiso for the stirrers, so they don't fall out easily. For both the frying pan and pot, I use Magic Hands, which have detachable handles. I can load large frying pans and pots without any problems. (Tefal is expensive, so I've been using the cheaper Magic Hands. I've had them for over a year, and they're great because the coating doesn't peel off even when I run the dishwasher hard.) The drilled holes are 6mm. The installer was very friendly and installed quickly. When I used the Chefbone 6-seater, no-installation dishwasher, I used to fill it with a 20-liter water tank, and since I didn't find that particularly inconvenient, I asked if I could use a water tank to avoid drilling holes. The technician said it wasn't possible. If it were possible, they would have sold it as a no-installation dishwasher, right? No-installation dishwashers have a water-sucking function. This one should automatically draw water in. If you have a water purifier, you can connect it there. I don't have a water purifier, so I drilled a hole in the marble countertop where it's not easily visible and connected it under the sink. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher. Naturally, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person dishwasher. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? Everything falls under the dishes. You have to place them tightly, horizontally and vertically, to even fit small dishes. Seriously, there are just long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are so big that rice bowls fall through. I'm only supposed to put in large dishes, but there's no room for them. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. I can't cut it up, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and the price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that would never come off no matter how hard I scrubbed will disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin the fish you ate. You don't need to pre-wash the fatty pork belly. 80% of dishwashers are detergent-washed.) The good thing is that there's no separate place to insert the cutlery holder, so you can move it to the innermost, outermost, middle, or wherever you want. (The Cheffubon had a fixed place to insert it, so it was really inconvenient.) If you put a frying pan or pot on the left, the dishes on the upper left shelf won't clean well. Or maybe you should move it to the right. I think you need to play Tetris a little better. Dishwashers all have similar cleaning power, and the detergent makes a difference. The lack of a top nozzle definitely makes a difference in cleaning power. Still, if you're a first-time user, you probably won't notice any issues. The inside gets cleaned really well (since it's detergent-washing anyway). And those who just start the cycle won't feel much of a problem. You can put the dishes in the basket and run them while they're all oily. Those who downgrade like me might say, "Hmm." It's just that the outside isn't quite as clean when you touch it. It doesn't mean they're not washed well. They're bound to get better than hand washing anyway. Well, I'm not sure if this media dishwasher with a cascade function will clean them very well. I forgive it because it's cheap. The fan noise from the Chefborn was really annoying afterward. (The fan would run automatically for 72 hours, so even if I opened the door and turned off the power, the fan would run;; If I turned off the ventilation mode, the fan would stop running even if I turned off the power, but after I finished, the fan would always run, so I had to press the power button to turn it off, which was inconvenient.) It's actually nice that there's no such thing. I don't need the automatic door opening function. After I'm done, I usually leave the door open to dry it. (If you shake off any standing water, the dishes will dry very quickly because they're hot.) I'm not planning on using it for a long time, so I'm satisfied with it. For those who plan on using it for a long time, it would be better if the water stream came out from the top. Of course, it would be more expensive. Considering the price, this one isn't bad. I think spending more money on detergent would cover it to some extent. And it holds. It holds as much as the basket size. I only use frying pans, pots, and tall dishes, so it doesn't feel like it's full. If you use a lot of flat dishes, it seems like it would really hold a lot. Even if I put in just two large frying pans and pots, it's more than half full. (There's a cutlery holder and a little space in front of the detergent dispenser for dishes). It definitely holds less than a 12-person dishwasher. Two people eat three meals a day at home, so we only turn it once a day. We eat rice and don't eat side dishes, so that's understandable. When using a 12-person dishwasher, we soaked it in water and turned it once every three days. It doesn't seem to matter how many people live in a household or how many meals a day they eat. Each household uses different sizes and quantities of dishes, so roughly estimate how much you'll need before purchasing. I use the thick chopsticks sold at Daiso for the stirrers, so they don't fall out easily. For both the frying pan and pot, I use Magic Hands, which have detachable handles. I can load large frying pans and pots without any problems. (Tefal is expensive, so I've been using the cheaper Magic Hands. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. I used to use a 12-person dishwasher, but I downgraded to a 6-person dishwasher. Naturally, it doesn't clean as well as a 12-person dishwasher. I originally used Libre powder detergent, but I bought it with the intention of switching to a more powerful one. I also tried the Chefbone, a no-installation 6-person dishwasher. What the heck? Everything falls under the dishes. You have to place them tightly, horizontally and vertically, to even fit small dishes. Seriously, there are just long vertical lines on both sides. And the holes in the front are so big that rice bowls fall through. I'm only supposed to put in large dishes, but there's no room for them. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I bought a Cuckoo 6-person dishwasher, but then I found this Media Yo product, and it seemed exactly like the Cuckoo. The size, weight, and basket shape are all exactly the same. I used to buy Media from Cuckoo. Coupang seems to import and install Media products directly. However, Media is cheaper (about 220,000 won) and comes with a two-year warranty for Rocket installation. Cuckoo offers about 250,000 won, and it's a bit better if you connect with a customer service representative via KakaoTalk (I heard they don't connect by phone at all). It's a one-on-one chat service, but you have to wait 7-9 minutes for a response per message. And after-sales service is also free, with a basic one-year warranty, or 1 year and 6 months if you verify something on the official website. It's also a hassle to call an installer every time. So, I decided to forgo Cuckoo altogether and bought Media. The pros? It's cheap. The cons? Because it's cheap, it doesn't have a top nozzle, so it's not as easy to clean. I just put a frying pan and a pot in it and spin it (just like I've used a dishwasher). However, because the water doesn't flow from above, the outside of the frying pan doesn't get cleaned properly, and it doesn't clean every nook and cranny perfectly. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. For 12 people, 1 frosh is enough, and for 6 people, 1/2 is enough. If you use too much detergent, the water may smell fishy.) I used Cascade Platinum, but it smells strong. I can't cut it up, so I don't use it now. (Lemon? If you're okay with the smell and the price, use Cascade Platinum. Even black tea stains that would never come off no matter how hard I scrubbed will disappear. There's no fishy smell even if you spin the fish you ate. You don't need to pre-wash the fatty pork belly. 80% of dishwashers are detergent-washed.) The good thing is that there's no separate place to insert the cutlery holder, so you can move it to the innermost, outermost, middle, or wherever you want. (The Cheffubon had a fixed place to insert it, so it was really inconvenient.) If you put a frying pan or pot on the left, the dishes on the upper left shelf won't clean well. Or maybe you should move it to the right. I think you need to play Tetris a little better. Dishwashers all have similar cleaning power, and the detergent makes a difference. The lack of a top nozzle definitely makes a difference in cleaning power. Still, if you're a first-time user, you probably won't notice any issues. The inside gets cleaned really well (since it's detergent-washing anyway). And those who just start the cycle won't feel much of a problem. You can put the dishes in the basket and run them while they're all oily. Those who downgrade like me might say, "Hmm." It's just that the outside isn't quite as clean when you touch it. It doesn't mean they're not washed well. They're bound to get better than hand washing anyway. Well, I'm not sure if this media dishwasher with a cascade function will clean them very well. I forgive it because it's cheap. The fan noise from the Chefborn was really annoying afterward. (The fan would run automatically for 72 hours, so even if I opened the door and turned off the power, the fan would run;; If I turned off the ventilation mode, the fan would stop running even if I turned off the power, but after I finished, the fan would always run, so I had to press the power button to turn it off, which was inconvenient.) It's actually nice that there's no such thing. I don't need the automatic door opening function. After I'm done, I usually leave the door open to dry it. (If you shake off any standing water, the dishes will dry very quickly because they're hot.) I'm not planning on using it for a long time, so I'm satisfied with it. For those who plan on using it for a long time, it would be better if the water stream came out from the top. Of course, it would be more expensive. Considering the price, this one isn't bad. I think spending more money on detergent would cover it to some extent. And it holds. It holds as much as the basket size. I only use frying pans, pots, and tall dishes, so it doesn't feel like it's full. If you use a lot of flat dishes, it seems like it would really hold a lot. Even if I put in just two large frying pans and pots, it's more than half full. (There's a cutlery holder and a little space in front of the detergent dispenser for dishes). It definitely holds less than a 12-person dishwasher. Two people eat three meals a day at home, so we only turn it once a day. We eat rice and don't eat side dishes, so that's understandable. When using a 12-person dishwasher, we soaked it in water and turned it once every three days. It doesn't seem to matter how many people live in a household or how many meals a day they eat. Each household uses different sizes and quantities of dishes, so roughly estimate how much you'll need before purchasing. I use the thick chopsticks sold at Daiso for the stirrers, so they don't fall out easily. For both the frying pan and pot, I use Magic Hands, which have detachable handles. I can load large frying pans and pots without any problems. (Tefal is expensive, so I've been using the cheaper Magic Hands. I've had them for over a year, and they're great because the coating doesn't peel off even when I run the dishwasher hard.) The drilled holes are 6mm. The installer was very friendly and installed quickly. When I used the Chefbone 6-seater, no-installation dishwasher, I used to fill it with a 20-liter water tank, and since I didn't find that particularly inconvenient, I asked if I could use a water tank to avoid drilling holes. The technician said it wasn't possible. If it were possible, they would have sold it as a no-installation dishwasher, right? No-installation dishwashers have a water-sucking function. This one should automatically draw water in. If you have a water purifier, you can connect it there. Comments (English): [ I'm leaving a genuine review. ] || ---------------- || This is my honest review after using several dishwashers. If I put a large dish in, it blocks the detergent drawer door, or it pops out and prevents the door from closing. Seriously, I couldn't use it. I use Frosh baking soda as a detergent. (If it's not oily, 1/4 will clean it well. If it's oily, 1/2 to 1/3 will clean it well. You don't need to use all of it. Sentence (English): We ordered this dishwasher for our guest apartment.
Comments (English): [ Good device - but where there is light, there is also shadow. ] || ---------------- || We ordered this dishwasher for our guest apartment. It had to be a BSH model with an automatic program. The dishwasher was delivered last week and installed without any problems. Since we already have BSH appliances in the house, operating it is no issue. The smart home option was a nice bonus, but it does have the advantage of allowing you to, for example, download additional programs and assign different settings to the favorites button. I've assigned a glass program there. So it's a neat feature that you can definitely get used to. The dishwasher is very quiet and otherwise does what it's supposed to. Thanks to the "Turbo" button and "Extra Dry" setting, you can even override the "Eco" mode and don't have to wait four hours for your dishes to come out dry. HOWEVER, a funnel for refilling the salt used to be standard equipment on every BSH dishwasher. This has already fallen victim to cost-cutting measures. Just like the tiered racks in the upper basket shown in all the pictures and in the manual. Presumably, you can "reorder" all of this in the app's shop, but this kind of thing should really be standard and included with a branded device from a German manufacturer. Therefore, one point deducted!
Comments (Original): [ Gutes Gerät - wo Licht ist, da ist auch Schatten ] || ---------------- || Haben uns dieses Gerät für unsere Gästewohnung bestellt. Es sollte ein Gerät von BSH sein, welches ein Automatikprogramm hat. Das Gerät wurde letzte Woche geliefert und auch ohne Komplikationen angeschlossen. Da wir schon BSH Geräte im Haus haben, ist die Bedienung kein Problem. Die Smarthome Option war jetzt ein 'nice to have', hat aber den Vorteil, dass man z.B. noch Programme nachladen kann und somit auf die Favoritentaste verschiedene Einstellungen legen kann. Ich hab dort ein Glasprogramm drauf gelegt. Also das ist schon eine nette Spielerei, an die man sich sicher gewöhnen kann. Das Gerät ist sehr leise und macht ansonsten das was es soll. Dank 'Turbotaste' und 'Extratrocken', kann man auch den 'Eco'-Modus überlisten und muss nicht 4h auf sein Geschirr warten und es ist zum Schluss auch trocken. Sentence (English): We run it every day, due to having a lot of baby bottles and pump parts.
Comments (English): [ Great features and versatility ] || ---------------- || We run it every day, due to having a lot of baby bottles and pump parts. I love the versatility of the fold down sections and the height adjustment on the second level. The third rack is even more useful than I expected. We can put small pump parts, and other very small items, up there that we never could have put in our old dishwasher. We typically use the normal wash with steam and night dry. Really on the fence with this purchase, but not much I can do about it.

Sentence (English): I was able to use it as a good opportunity.
Comments (English): I was thinking about whether to buy a dishwasher or a dryer after moving. I was able to use it as a good opportunity. The colors are just my taste in black and white. It is neat and simple. The size is bigger than I thought. First of all, it was good because it was self-installation and easy to install. The standard took about an hour and the fast took about 30 minutes. However, it may be a little inconvenient because it doesn't dry. There is no separate drying function. You have to use the standard to finish drying. After finishing, you have to leave the door open. There is no auto-opening function. Since it is cheap, there is no choice~~ It washes well with steam sterilization. The operating noise is loud, but it is a new world. The size is just right for a family of two. When there are not many dishes, it is sometimes a little ambiguous to use. I wonder how much the electricity bill will be if I think about running it for 1 hour on the standard basis. I wash dishes in hot water for grease, but now I don't have to worry about grease anymore. Fact check. From messy sauce to stuck-on rice to grease that can't be cleaned, it's a 72-hour ventilation circulation system product that dries and safely stores everything at once. The fan inside improves the drying function, and the airflow generated for 72 hours removes moisture and odor, allowing you to store dishes easily without separate organization. Moisture/odor fan operation cycle Standard, strong mode (not fast mode) 72 High temperature water to clean grease stains Midea 72 degrees Celsius high temperature washing Grease removal Check with your own eyes to see if it is cleaned cleanly! No other functions are needed. 5 practical washing modes With various washing modes that only contain the functions you need, leave the dishwasher to wash the dishes and spend your time leisurely! 5 washing modes Standard Strong Eco Fast Don't worry about water overflowing! Automatic water level recognition sensor When the water tank inside is full, the water level is automatically notified. Fill the water before using the dishwasher and select the course. Space-saving design No drilling or installation anywhere Water supply is available without restrictions on the side or upper space, so you can use it anywhere without inconvenience. If the water supply drainage is possible, use it without space restrictions. You can use it anywhere, under the sink or under the upper cabinet. Even though it is small, it can hold a lot. Storage space optimized for 2~3 households. Don't put off the annoying dishwashing and leave it to the dishwasher with the dish storage space optimized for 2~3 person households. Sentence (English): The size is bigger than I thought.
Comments (English): I was thinking about whether to buy a dishwasher or a dryer after moving. I was able to use it as a good opportunity. The colors are just my taste in black and white. It is neat and simple. The size is bigger than I thought. First of all, it was good because it was self-installation and easy to install. The standard took about an hour and the fast took about 30 minutes. However, it may be a little inconvenient because it doesn't dry. There is no separate drying function. You have to use the standard to finish drying. After finishing, you have to leave the door open. There is no auto-opening function. Since it is cheap, there is no choice~~ It washes well with steam sterilization. The operating noise is loud, but it is a new world. The size is just right for a family of two. When there are not many dishes, it is sometimes a little ambiguous to use. I wonder how much the electricity bill will be if I think about running it for 1 hour on the standard basis. I wash dishes in hot water for grease, but now I don't have to worry about grease anymore. Fact check. From messy sauce to stuck-on rice to grease that can't be cleaned, it's a 72-hour ventilation circulation system product that dries and safely stores everything at once. The fan inside improves the drying function, and the airflow generated for 72 hours removes moisture and odor, allowing you to store dishes easily without separate organization. Moisture/odor fan operation cycle Standard, strong mode (not fast mode) 72 High temperature water to clean grease stains Midea 72 degrees Celsius high temperature washing Grease removal Check with your own eyes to see if it is cleaned cleanly! No other functions are needed. 5 practical washing modes With various washing modes that only contain the functions you need, leave the dishwasher to wash the dishes and spend your time leisurely! 5 washing modes Standard Strong Eco Fast Don't worry about water overflowing! Automatic water level recognition sensor When the water tank inside is full, the water level is automatically notified. Fill the water before using the dishwasher and select the course. Space-saving design No drilling or installation anywhere Water supply is available without restrictions on the side or upper space, so you can use it anywhere without inconvenience. If the water supply drainage is possible, use it without space restrictions. You can use it anywhere, under the sink or under the upper cabinet. Even though it is small, it can hold a lot. Storage space optimized for 2~3 households. Don't put off the annoying dishwashing and leave it to the dishwasher with the dish storage space optimized for 2~3 person households. Comments (English): I was thinking about whether to buy a dishwasher or a dryer after moving. I was able to use it as a good opportunity. The colors are just my taste in black and white. It is neat and simple. The size is bigger than I thought. First of all, it was good because it was self-installation and easy to install. The standard took about an hour and the fast took about 30 minutes. However, it may be a little inconvenient because it doesn't dry. There is no separate drying function. You have to use the standard to finish drying. After finishing, you have to leave the door open. There is no auto-opening function. Since it is cheap, there is no choice~~ It washes well with steam sterilization. The operating noise is loud, but it is a new world. The size is just right for a family of two. When there are not many dishes, it is sometimes a little ambiguous to use. I wonder how much the electricity bill will be if I think about running it for 1 hour on the standard basis. I wash dishes in hot water for grease, but now I don't have to worry about grease anymore. Fact check. From messy sauce to stuck-on rice to grease that can't be cleaned, it's a 72-hour ventilation circulation system product that dries and safely stores everything at once. The fan inside improves the drying function, and the airflow generated for 72 hours removes moisture and odor, allowing you to store dishes easily without separate organization. Moisture/odor fan operation cycle Standard, strong mode (not fast mode) 72 High temperature water to clean grease stains Midea 72 degrees Celsius high temperature washing Grease removal Check with your own eyes to see if it is cleaned cleanly! No other functions are needed. 5 practical washing modes With various washing modes that only contain the functions you need, leave the dishwasher to wash the dishes and spend your time leisurely! 5 washing modes Standard Strong Eco Fast Don't worry about water overflowing! Automatic water level recognition sensor When the water tank inside is full, the water level is automatically notified. Fill the water before using the dishwasher and select the course. Space-saving design No drilling or installation anywhere Water supply is available without restrictions on the side or upper space, so you can use it anywhere without inconvenience. Storage space optimized for 2~3 households. Don't put off the annoying dishwashing and leave it to the dishwasher with the dish storage space optimized for 2~3 person households. Sentence (English): You have to use the standard to finish drying.
Comments (English): I was thinking about whether to buy a dishwasher or a dryer after moving. I was able to use it as a good opportunity. The colors are just my taste in black and white. The standard took about an hour and the fast took about 30 minutes. However, it may be a little inconvenient because it doesn't dry. There is no separate drying function. You have to use the standard to finish drying. After finishing, you have to leave the door open. There is no auto-opening function. Since it is cheap, there is no choice~~ It washes well with steam sterilization. The operating noise is loud, but it is a new world. The size is just right for a family of two. When there are not many dishes, it is sometimes a little ambiguous to use. I wonder how much the electricity bill will be if I think about running it for 1 hour on the standard basis. I wash dishes in hot water for grease, but now I don't have to worry about grease anymore. Fact check. From messy sauce to stuck-on rice to grease that can't be cleaned, it's a 72-hour ventilation circulation system product that dries and safely stores everything at once. The fan inside improves the drying function, and the airflow generated for 72 hours removes moisture and odor, allowing you to store dishes easily without separate organization. Moisture/odor fan operation cycle Standard, strong mode (not fast mode) 72 High temperature water to clean grease stains Midea 72 degrees Celsius high temperature washing Grease removal Check with your own eyes to see if it is cleaned cleanly! Automatic water level recognition sensor When the water tank inside is full, the water level is automatically notified. Fill the water before using the dishwasher and select the course. Space-saving design No drilling or installation anywhere Water supply is available without restrictions on the side or upper space, so you can use it anywhere without inconvenience. Sentence (English): Since it is cheap, there is no choice~~ It washes well with steam sterilization.
Comments (English): I was thinking about whether to buy a dishwasher or a dryer after moving. I was able to use it as a good opportunity. The colors are just my taste in black and white. It is neat and simple. The size is bigger than I thought. First of all, it was good because it was self-installation and easy to install. The standard took about an hour and the fast took about 30 minutes. However, it may be a little inconvenient because it doesn't dry. There is no separate drying function. You have to use the standard to finish drying. After finishing, you have to leave the door open. There is no auto-opening function. Since it is cheap, there is no choice~~ It washes well with steam sterilization. The operating noise is loud, but it is a new world. The size is just right for a family of two. When there are not many dishes, it is sometimes a little ambiguous to use. I wonder how much the electricity bill will be if I think about running it for 1 hour on the standard basis. I wash dishes in hot water for grease, but now I don't have to worry about grease anymore. Fact check. From messy sauce to stuck-on rice to grease that can't be cleaned, it's a 72-hour ventilation circulation system product that dries and safely stores everything at once. The fan inside improves the drying function, and the airflow generated for 72 hours removes moisture and odor, allowing you to store dishes easily without separate organization. Moisture/odor fan operation cycle Standard, strong mode (not fast mode) 72 High temperature water to clean grease stains Midea 72 degrees Celsius high temperature washing Grease removal Check with your own eyes to see if it is cleaned cleanly! No other functions are needed. 5 practical washing modes With various washing modes that only contain the functions you need, leave the dishwasher to wash the dishes and spend your time leisurely! 5 washing modes Standard Strong Eco Fast Don't worry about water overflowing! Automatic water level recognition sensor When the water tank inside is full, the water level is automatically notified. Fill the water before using the dishwasher and select the course. Space-saving design No drilling or installation anywhere Water supply is available without restrictions on the side or upper space, so you can use it anywhere without inconvenience. If the water supply drainage is possible, use it without space restrictions. You can use it anywhere, under the sink or under the upper cabinet. Even though it is small, it can hold a lot. Storage space optimized for 2~3 households. Don't put off the annoying dishwashing and leave it to the dishwasher with the dish storage space optimized for 2~3 person households. Sentence (English): The size is just right for a family of two.
Comments (English): I was thinking about whether to buy a dishwasher or a dryer after moving. I was able to use it as a good opportunity. The colors are just my taste in black and white. It is neat and simple. The size is bigger than I thought. First of all, it was good because it was self-installation and easy to install. The standard took about an hour and the fast took about 30 minutes. However, it may be a little inconvenient because it doesn't dry. There is no separate drying function. You have to use the standard to finish drying. After finishing, you have to leave the door open. There is no auto-opening function. Since it is cheap, there is no choice~~ It washes well with steam sterilization. The operating noise is loud, but it is a new world. The size is just right for a family of two. When there are not many dishes, it is sometimes a little ambiguous to use. I wonder how much the electricity bill will be if I think about running it for 1 hour on the standard basis. I wash dishes in hot water for grease, but now I don't have to worry about grease anymore. Fact check. From messy sauce to stuck-on rice to grease that can't be cleaned, it's a 72-hour ventilation circulation system product that dries and safely stores everything at once. The fan inside improves the drying function, and the airflow generated for 72 hours removes moisture and odor, allowing you to store dishes easily without separate organization. Moisture/odor fan operation cycle Standard, strong mode (not fast mode) 72 High temperature water to clean grease stains Midea 72 degrees Celsius high temperature washing Grease removal Check with your own eyes to see if it is cleaned cleanly! No other functions are needed. 5 practical washing modes With various washing modes that only contain the functions you need, leave the dishwasher to wash the dishes and spend your time leisurely! 5 washing modes Standard Strong Eco Fast Don't worry about water overflowing! Automatic water level recognition sensor When the water tank inside is full, the water level is automatically notified. Fill the water before using the dishwasher and select the course. Space-saving design No drilling or installation anywhere Water supply is available without restrictions on the side or upper space, so you can use it anywhere without inconvenience. If the water supply drainage is possible, use it without space restrictions. You can use it anywhere, under the sink or under the upper cabinet. Even though it is small, it can hold a lot. Storage space optimized for 2~3 households. Don't put off the annoying dishwashing and leave it to the dishwasher with the dish storage space optimized for 2~3 person households. Sentence (English): I wash dishes in hot water for grease, but now I don't have to worry about grease anymore.
Comments (English): I was thinking about whether to buy a dishwasher or a dryer after moving. I was able to use it as a good opportunity. The colors are just my taste in black and white. It is neat and simple. The size is bigger than I thought. First of all, it was good because it was self-installation and easy to install. The standard took about an hour and the fast took about 30 minutes. However, it may be a little inconvenient because it doesn't dry. There is no separate drying function. You have to use the standard to finish drying. After finishing, you have to leave the door open. There is no auto-opening function. Since it is cheap, there is no choice~~ It washes well with steam sterilization. The operating noise is loud, but it is a new world. The size is just right for a family of two. When there are not many dishes, it is sometimes a little ambiguous to use. I wonder how much the electricity bill will be if I think about running it for 1 hour on the standard basis. I wash dishes in hot water for grease, but now I don't have to worry about grease anymore. Fact check. From messy sauce to stuck-on rice to grease that can't be cleaned, it's a 72-hour ventilation circulation system product that dries and safely stores everything at once. The fan inside improves the drying function, and the airflow generated for 72 hours removes moisture and odor, allowing you to store dishes easily without separate organization. Moisture/odor fan operation cycle Standard, strong mode (not fast mode) 72 High temperature water to clean grease stains Midea 72 degrees Celsius high temperature washing Grease removal Check with your own eyes to see if it is cleaned cleanly! No other functions are needed. 5 practical washing modes With various washing modes that only contain the functions you need, leave the dishwasher to wash the dishes and spend your time leisurely! 5 washing modes Standard Strong Eco Fast Don't worry about water overflowing! Automatic water level recognition sensor When the water tank inside is full, the water level is automatically notified. Fill the water before using the dishwasher and select the course. Space-saving design No drilling or installation anywhere Water supply is available without restrictions on the side or upper space, so you can use it anywhere without inconvenience. Sentence (English): The fan inside improves the drying function, and the airflow generated for 72 hours removes moisture and odor, allowing you to store dishes easily without separate organization.
Comments (English): I was thinking about whether to buy a dishwasher or a dryer after moving. I was able to use it as a good opportunity. The colors are just my taste in black and white. It is neat and simple. The size is bigger than I thought. First of all, it was good because it was self-installation and easy to install. The standard took about an hour and the fast took about 30 minutes. However, it may be a little inconvenient because it doesn't dry. There is no separate drying function. You have to use the standard to finish drying. After finishing, you have to leave the door open. There is no auto-opening function. Since it is cheap, there is no choice~~ It washes well with steam sterilization. The operating noise is loud, but it is a new world. The size is just right for a family of two. When there are not many dishes, it is sometimes a little ambiguous to use. I wonder how much the electricity bill will be if I think about running it for 1 hour on the standard basis. I wash dishes in hot water for grease, but now I don't have to worry about grease anymore. Fact check. From messy sauce to stuck-on rice to grease that can't be cleaned, it's a 72-hour ventilation circulation system product that dries and safely stores everything at once. The fan inside improves the drying function, and the airflow generated for 72 hours removes moisture and odor, allowing you to store dishes easily without separate organization. Moisture/odor fan operation cycle Standard, strong mode (not fast mode) 72 High temperature water to clean grease stains Midea 72 degrees Celsius high temperature washing Grease removal Check with your own eyes to see if it is cleaned cleanly! No other functions are needed. 5 practical washing modes With various washing modes that only contain the functions you need, leave the dishwasher to wash the dishes and spend your time leisurely! 5 washing modes Standard Strong Eco Fast Don't worry about water overflowing! Automatic water level recognition sensor When the water tank inside is full, the water level is automatically notified. Fill the water before using the dishwasher and select the course. Space-saving design No drilling or installation anywhere Water supply is available without restrictions on the side or upper space, so you can use it anywhere without inconvenience. If the water supply drainage is possible, use it without space restrictions. You can use it anywhere, under the sink or under the upper cabinet. Even though it is small, it can hold a lot. Storage space optimized for 2~3 households. Don't put off the annoying dishwashing and leave it to the dishwasher with the dish storage space optimized for 2~3 person households. Sentence (English): 5 practical washing modes With various washing modes that only contain the functions you need, leave the dishwasher to wash the dishes and spend your time leisurely!
Comments (English): I was thinking about whether to buy a dishwasher or a dryer after moving. I was able to use it as a good opportunity. The colors are just my taste in black and white. It is neat and simple. The size is bigger than I thought. First of all, it was good because it was self-installation and easy to install. The standard took about an hour and the fast took about 30 minutes. However, it may be a little inconvenient because it doesn't dry. There is no separate drying function. You have to use the standard to finish drying. After finishing, you have to leave the door open. There is no auto-opening function. Since it is cheap, there is no choice~~ It washes well with steam sterilization. The operating noise is loud, but it is a new world. The size is just right for a family of two. When there are not many dishes, it is sometimes a little ambiguous to use. I wonder how much the electricity bill will be if I think about running it for 1 hour on the standard basis. I wash dishes in hot water for grease, but now I don't have to worry about grease anymore. Fact check. From messy sauce to stuck-on rice to grease that can't be cleaned, it's a 72-hour ventilation circulation system product that dries and safely stores everything at once. The fan inside improves the drying function, and the airflow generated for 72 hours removes moisture and odor, allowing you to store dishes easily without separate organization. Moisture/odor fan operation cycle Standard, strong mode (not fast mode) 72 High temperature water to clean grease stains Midea 72 degrees Celsius high temperature washing Grease removal Check with your own eyes to see if it is cleaned cleanly! No other functions are needed. 5 practical washing modes With various washing modes that only contain the functions you need, leave the dishwasher to wash the dishes and spend your time leisurely! 5 washing modes Standard Strong Eco Fast Don't worry about water overflowing! Automatic water level recognition sensor When the water tank inside is full, the water level is automatically notified. Fill the water before using the dishwasher and select the course. Space-saving design No drilling or installation anywhere Water supply is available without restrictions on the side or upper space, so you can use it anywhere without inconvenience. Sentence (English): Fill the water before using the dishwasher and select the course.
Comments (English): I was thinking about whether to buy a dishwasher or a dryer after moving. I was able to use it as a good opportunity. The colors are just my taste in black and white. It is neat and simple. The size is bigger than I thought. First of all, it was good because it was self-installation and easy to install. The standard took about an hour and the fast took about 30 minutes. However, it may be a little inconvenient because it doesn't dry. There is no separate drying function. You have to use the standard to finish drying. After finishing, you have to leave the door open. There is no auto-opening function. Since it is cheap, there is no choice~~ It washes well with steam sterilization. The operating noise is loud, but it is a new world. The size is just right for a family of two. When there are not many dishes, it is sometimes a little ambiguous to use. I wonder how much the electricity bill will be if I think about running it for 1 hour on the standard basis. I wash dishes in hot water for grease, but now I don't have to worry about grease anymore. Fact check. From messy sauce to stuck-on rice to grease that can't be cleaned, it's a 72-hour ventilation circulation system product that dries and safely stores everything at once. The fan inside improves the drying function, and the airflow generated for 72 hours removes moisture and odor, allowing you to store dishes easily without separate organization. Moisture/odor fan operation cycle Standard, strong mode (not fast mode) 72 High temperature water to clean grease stains Midea 72 degrees Celsius high temperature washing Grease removal Check with your own eyes to see if it is cleaned cleanly! No other functions are needed. 5 practical washing modes With various washing modes that only contain the functions you need, leave the dishwasher to wash the dishes and spend your time leisurely! 5 washing modes Standard Strong Eco Fast Don't worry about water overflowing! Automatic water level recognition sensor When the water tank inside is full, the water level is automatically notified. Fill the water before using the dishwasher and select the course. Space-saving design No drilling or installation anywhere Water supply is available without restrictions on the side or upper space, so you can use it anywhere without inconvenience. If the water supply drainage is possible, use it without space restrictions. You can use it anywhere, under the sink or under the upper cabinet. Even though it is small, it can hold a lot. Storage space optimized for 2~3 households. Don't put off the annoying dishwashing and leave it to the dishwasher with the dish storage space optimized for 2~3 person households. Comments (English): I was thinking about whether to buy a dishwasher or a dryer after moving. I was able to use it as a good opportunity. The colors are just my taste in black and white. Since it is cheap, there is no choice~~ It washes well with steam sterilization. The operating noise is loud, but it is a new world. The size is just right for a family of two. I wash dishes in hot water for grease, but now I don't have to worry about grease anymore. Fact check. From messy sauce to stuck-on rice to grease that can't be cleaned, it's a 72-hour ventilation circulation system product that dries and safely stores everything at once. Sentence (English): Don't put off the annoying dishwashing and leave it to the dishwasher with the dish storage space optimized for 2~3 person households.
Comments (English): I was thinking about whether to buy a dishwasher or a dryer after moving. I was able to use it as a good opportunity. The colors are just my taste in black and white. It is neat and simple. The size is bigger than I thought. First of all, it was good because it was self-installation and easy to install. The standard took about an hour and the fast took about 30 minutes. However, it may be a little inconvenient because it doesn't dry. There is no separate drying function. You have to use the standard to finish drying. After finishing, you have to leave the door open. There is no auto-opening function. Since it is cheap, there is no choice~~ It washes well with steam sterilization. The operating noise is loud, but it is a new world. The size is just right for a family of two. When there are not many dishes, it is sometimes a little ambiguous to use. I wonder how much the electricity bill will be if I think about running it for 1 hour on the standard basis. I wash dishes in hot water for grease, but now I don't have to worry about grease anymore. Fact check. From messy sauce to stuck-on rice to grease that can't be cleaned, it's a 72-hour ventilation circulation system product that dries and safely stores everything at once. The fan inside improves the drying function, and the airflow generated for 72 hours removes moisture and odor, allowing you to store dishes easily without separate organization. Moisture/odor fan operation cycle Standard, strong mode (not fast mode) 72 High temperature water to clean grease stains Midea 72 degrees Celsius high temperature washing Grease removal Check with your own eyes to see if it is cleaned cleanly! No other functions are needed. 5 practical washing modes With various washing modes that only contain the functions you need, leave the dishwasher to wash the dishes and spend your time leisurely! 5 washing modes Standard Strong Eco Fast Don't worry about water overflowing! Automatic water level recognition sensor When the water tank inside is full, the water level is automatically notified. Fill the water before using the dishwasher and select the course. Space-saving design No drilling or installation anywhere Water supply is available without restrictions on the side or upper space, so you can use it anywhere without inconvenience. If the water supply drainage is possible, use it without space restrictions. You can use it anywhere, under the sink or under the upper cabinet. Even though it is small, it can hold a lot. Storage space optimized for 2~3 households. Don't put off the annoying dishwashing and leave it to the dishwasher with the dish storage space optimized for 2~3 person households.
